name: SirixDB
tagline: Embeddable bitemporal database that keeps every revision of JSON and XML resources queryable.
description: SirixDB is a log-structured, copy-on-write store that grew out of the University of Konstanz Treetank research project. Every commit produces a cheap immutable snapshot through page-level versioning and structural sharing, so you can query any past revision, diff two revisions, or ask how a document looked at a given valid time. Queries use JSONiq/XQuery through the Brackit engine with temporal extensions, and it runs either in-process as a single JAR or as a Vert.x REST server with Docker images. It is actively developed but still labelled 1.0 beta, which makes it a good fit for audit-heavy and time-travel use cases or research into versioned storage rather than general-purpose OLTP.
developer: SirixDB open-source project (University of Konstanz origins)

scale.notes: Single-node store; history grows with every revision, so plan disk for retained versions.

strengths: Every commit is an immutable, queryable snapshot; revision diffs and point-in-time queries are built in
Page-level copy-on-write versioning keeps the cost of history far below full copies
Bitemporal: tracks both transaction time and valid time
Embeds as a single JAR or runs as a REST server with Docker images
Permissive BSD-3 license and an actively maintained codebase
weaknesses: Still a 1.0 beta after more than a decade, so APIs and on-disk format can change
Small community and few public production references
One writer per resource limits write concurrency
JSONiq/XQuery is unfamiliar to most application teams
useCases: Audit trails that must reconstruct any past state
Versioned JSON or XML document storage
Research and teaching on versioned storage engines
notIdealFor: Write-heavy OLTP with many concurrent writers
Teams that need SQL and mainstream BI tooling
